goldens.comment: Unsafe raw List deserialization without type safety. Calling Optional.get() directly on the Optional returned by RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without checking isPresent() can lead to a NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:338 — isValid`'s recovery-code branch only does `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` and never removes/marks the matched code or writes back to `myUser.recoveryCodes`, so a single recovery code can be replayed to log in an unlimited number of times for user-storage-backed users.

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...)`, the newly added RecoveryAuthnCodes branch deserializes the stored list and only checks `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`, returning true without mutating `myUser.recoveryCodes` or persisting a reduced/marked list. The diff shows no other write-back in this provider on successful validation, so within this user-storage implementation a matching recovery code would remain valid for subsequent logins (replay).

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/storage/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.java:500 — testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` only logs in once with a fresh code and never retries the same code (or asserts it was consumed/removed from storage), so the test passes identically whether or not recovery codes are single-use, silently masking the reuse bug in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid`.

adjudication.rationale: In the added test `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin`, the flow performs a single successful login using one recovery code (`enterRecoveryCodes(...); clickSignInButton();`) and never attempts a second login reusing the same code, nor does it assert any change/removal of the used code from storage. As a result, the test would still pass even if recovery codes were incorrectly reusable. This matters because the new `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid` implementation for recovery codes only checks `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(...)` and does not consume/remove the used code, so a single-use semantics regression would not be detected by this test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:116 — Hardcodes the provider id literal "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes" instead of referencing RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID, whose import was removed from the caller in this same diff, creating a fragile magic-string coupling.

adjudication.rationale: In the added method `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, the provider is fetched via a hardcoded literal: `session.getProvider(CredentialProvider.class, "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes")`. In the same diff, `RecoveryAuthnCodesAction` removes use/import of `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID` and instead calls this helper, so the constant is no longer referenced anywhere here. This isn’t a directly verifiable functional bug (the literal may match the real provider id), but it is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability issue introducing magic-string coupling that can break if the provider id changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/forms/login/freemarker/model/RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean.java:19 — credentialModelOpt.get() is called without checking isPresent(), so if RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) returns empty (e.g. because getCredentials silently swallowed a deserialization IOException) the constructor throws an unchecked NoSuchElementException instead of a graceful error

adjudication.rationale: In RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean, the constructor now calls `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` and then immediately dereferences it via `credentialModelOpt.get()` without checking `isPresent()`. From the diff, `getCredential()` can legitimately return `Optional.empty()` when neither federated nor local recovery-code credentials exist, and the new BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage `getCredentials()` can also omit the credential on deserialization `IOException` (it logs and does not add it). In those cases the constructor would throw `NoSuchElementException`, i.e., a real runtime failure rather than a handled/controlled error path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/forms/login/freemarker/model/RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean.java:21 — getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() is unguarded, so if all recovery codes are already used/exhausted the constructor throws an unchecked NoSuchElementException rather than handling the exhausted-codes case gracefully

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean`, the constructor does `recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get().getNumber();` (and also `credentialModelOpt.get()`), both of which are unguarded `Optional.get()` calls. If `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode()` returns `Optional.empty()` (e.g., no remaining recovery codes), this will throw `NoSuchElementException` at runtime rather than handling the exhausted-codes case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/storage/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.java:241 — testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only enters one never-before-used recovery code and never attempts to reuse/replay an already-consumed code, so the requested consumed/invalid-code edge case is completely untested

adjudication.rationale: In the added test `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin`, the flow sets up recovery codes, then performs exactly one login using a single requested code via `enterRecoveryCodes(..., 0, recoveryKeys)` and `clickSignInButton()`. There is no follow-up attempt to authenticate again with the same already-used code, nor any assertion that reuse is rejected/treated as invalid. Given this PR introduces/extends recovery-code handling (e.g., `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential` and `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` integration into the login flow), the absence of a replay/consumed-code negative test is a specific, diff-grounded test gap rather than a directly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/storage/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.java:241 — New test never submits a wrong/garbage recovery code for a user-storage-backed user to verify the INVALID_CREDENTIALS failureChallenge path still works with the new getCredential() lookup

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new lookup logic via `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` (checks federated credentials first, then local stored) and updates `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` to use it. The newly added test `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin()` in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest` only exercises the happy path by entering a valid recovery code (`enterRecoveryCodes(...generatedRecoveryAuthnCodes.get(requestedCode))`) and asserting successful login; it never submits an invalid/garbage code to assert the authenticator’s `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` failureChallenge behavior still works with the new cross-storage lookup. This is a concrete, diff-grounded testing gap for the newly introduced nontrivial behavior, but not a verifiable functional defect in the code itself.
